paper_metadata.title: Electric Power Demand Portfolio Optimization by Fermionic QAOA with Self-Consistent Local Field Modulation

summary: The paper studies a 20-variable electric power demand portfolio optimization problem using FQAOA-SCLFM on a noiseless qulacs simulator. Table I reports normalized expected costs of 0.074/0.046/0.018 for FQAOA-SCLFM at p=0/1/10, outperforming XY-QAOA (0.165/0.073/0.033) and prior FQAOA (0.168/0.066/0.026) across all eight time periods T = 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21.

experiments.description: Noiseless simulation study of FQAOA-SCLFM for electric power demand portfolio optimization across multiple time periods and QAOA depths, compared against XY-QAOA and prior FQAOA.

algorithm.variant: Fermionic QAOA with self-consistent local field modulation (FQAOA-SCLFM)
algorithm.ansatz: FQAOA ansatz with phase rotation and mixing unitaries; mixing unitary implemented as odd/even hopping layers, boundary-condition layer, and local-field Z rotations
algorithm.convergence_criteria: classical parameter optimization to minimize expected cost; HF self-consistent iteration converged for initial state preparation

hyperparameters.thop: set so first term of driver Hamiltonian cost range matches first term of cost Hamiltonian under constraints

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared via Hartree-Fock self-consistent iteration; variational parameters optimized classically (details of initial γ,β not reported)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One binary variable x_l per DR participant; computational basis state corresponds to bit string x in {0,1}^L
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize E_{t,x}=sum_{l,l'} sigma_{t,l,l'} x_l x_{l'} + (sum_l E[p_{t,l}] x_l - P'_{t,proc})^2 subject to sum_l x_l = M; time-averaged objective E_{T,x}=(1/N_T) sum_{t in T} E_{t,x} subject to sum_l x_l = M_T
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard constraint on fixed number of selected participants enforced by constant-particle-number subspace / XY-style mixer; procurement inequality handled by penalty term in objective via P'_{t,proc}=P_{t,proc}+delta/2
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_{p,T}=sum_{l,l'} sigma_{T,l,l'} n_l n_{l'} + (1/N_T) sum_{t in T} (P_t - P'_{t,proc})^2, with P_t=sum_l E[p_{t,l}] n_l; constraint operator C=sum_l n_l

problem_instance.description: Electric power demand portfolio optimization / negawatt trading using residential electricity usage data
problem_instance.dataset_name: Database of energy consumption in residences (Ref. [23])

dataset_specification.description: 20 residences in September 1-15, 2003; water-heater usage ignored; time periods T=3i for i=0..7 with three reference times each

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Expected negawatt E[p_{t,l}] and covariance sigma_{t,l,l'} estimated from historical residential electricity usage following Ref. [8]; mean covariance computed over each time period T
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Noiseless simulation; results reported for p=0,1,10 across all T values; cost distributions and expected costs compared against XY-QAOA and prior FQAOA

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: HF self-consistent iteration to determine initial state and local-field term; parameter scaling thop chosen to match cost ranges
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute Pt,tot, sigma_t,tot, and cost distribution D_T(E) from optimized state probabilities

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: HF energy decreases with iteration; oscillatory for alpha=0.8, stabilized for alpha<=0.6

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or wall-clock speedup analysis is provided; only empirical performance comparisons among quantum algorithms.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 20 logical qubits; QAOA depths p = 0, 1, 10; classical BFGS optimization; noiseless simulation on qulacs
limiting_factors: No QPU execution; only noiseless simulation
No asymptotic or constant-factor speedup analysis
Comparison is only against other quantum variants and a random-sampling baseline
Problem size is fixed at 20 participants/residences
Classical optimization and Hartree-Fock preprocessing dominate the workflow

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper states numerical simulations were performed using the fast quantum simulator qulacs and reports noiseless simulation results, with no real QPU named.
num_qubits inferred as 20 from the 20 DR participants / residences used as binary variables.
Circuit depth inferred only qualitatively from QAOA level p; the paper does not report an explicit depth number.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided; only empirical performance comparisons against classical optimization and prior quantum variants.
The paper reports improved expected cost for FQAOA-SCLFM over XY-QAOA and prior FQAOA, but only in noiseless simulation.
No practical quantum advantage over classical optimization is demonstrated.
